title: Rossdale Power Plant adaptive-reuse code and structural assessments
jurisdiction: City of Edmonton, Alberta (the Building and Fire Code Assessment explicitly names the City of Edmonton as AHJ)
code_edition: The Building and Fire Code Assessment uses the National Building Code – 2019 Alberta Edition and National Fire Code – 2019 Alberta Edition. The related RJC Structural Evaluation uses the National Building Code – 2019 Alberta Edition. These are historical editions; the challenge package basis is NBC(AE) 2023, 2nd printing.
document_date: Building and Fire Code Assessment submitted 2021-03-05, revised 2021-12-09; RJC Structural Evaluation dated 2022-08-08

facts.text: The City landing page lists the Building and Fire Code Assessment and Structural Evaluation among the Rossdale Power Plant project documents.
facts.locator: Official City of Edmonton project page, Project Documents accordion (landing-page HTML)

facts.text: The code assessment cover identifies the City of Edmonton as owner/client, Jensen Hughes as code consultant, and the architectural, heritage, structural/civil, and mechanical/electrical consultant team.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF p. 2 (report p. i)

facts.text: The project covers the Low Pressure Power Plant (Switch House, Turbine Hall, Boiler Hall), Pump Houses 1 and 2, and the ATCO Gas Building at 9469 Rossdale Ave W and 10155 96 Ave NW, Edmonton.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF p. 10 (report p. 2), §2.1

facts.text: The code assessment says it is conceptual and high-level, benchmarks against the 2019 Alberta code editions, and names the City of Edmonton as AHJ. It notes that design/construction must use the documents applicable at that later time.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF p. 11 (report p. 3), §§2.2–2.3

facts.text: The report evaluates a range of potential future major occupancies (Groups A1, A2, D, and E); it does not identify a selected future occupancy.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF pp. 9–10 (report pp. 1–2), §1.1 and §2.1

facts.text: Performance-based alternative approaches are described as options that could be considered later; they were outside the current scope, were not guaranteed to progress, require further evaluation, and remain subject to AHJ review.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF p. 12 (report p. 4), §2.7

facts.text: Potential investigations named by the code consultant include rationalizing exits, vestibules/pressurization, protected floor space, draft stops, combustible-content limits, and smoke ventilation analysis. They are exploratory possibilities, not selected or accepted solutions.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF p. 12 (report p. 4), §2.7; PDF p. 39 (report p. 31), Table 10-1

facts.text: The RJC report says available structural information was limited; its evaluation compared the existing Low Pressure Plant against the 2019 Alberta code and identifies change of use, higher expected snow loads, condition/load-path deficiencies, equipment removal, limited original-code information, and code changes as factors.
facts.locator: RJC Structural Evaluation, PDF p. 4 (printed report p. i), Executive Summary

facts.text: The RJC executive summary reports that some parts of the Low Pressure Plant did not meet the evaluated load demands and names the roofs, east-west lateral support, steel connections, and steel-plate floor areas among the deficiencies. It says the structure is not suitable for occupancy except very short-term controlled conditions, and describes repair/reinforcement and future City/AHJ decisions as next steps.
facts.locator: RJC Structural Evaluation, PDF pp. 4–5 (printed report pp. i–ii), Executive Summary

facts.text: The code assessment says existing exit-width measurements are approximate because doors were locked or padlocked during the site visit; it also records non-compliant exit conditions requiring further exploration.
facts.locator: Building and Fire Code Assessment, PDF p. 47 (report p. 39), exiting notes

limitations: This is one City of Edmonton adaptive-reuse project represented by two distinct consultant reports, not two separate projects or an original applicant submission.
Neither report is an alternative-solution application or permit decision. No accepted project-specific solution or approval was located.

The code assessment is expressly conceptual, covers potential rather than selected occupancies, and says alternative approaches are outside its current scope and subject to further analysis and AHJ review.
The reports use 2019 Alberta code editions; they do not establish requirements under the challenge package's NBC(AE) 2023 2nd printing basis or a later permit date.
The code assessment records approximate exiting measurements and locked/padlocked doors during the site visit. Some existing conditions and future project choices remain uncertain.

The RJC Structural Evaluation covers the Low Pressure Plant (Switch House, Turbine Hall, and Boiler Hall), not every Rossdale building; it identifies limited information and assumptions that later project phases must verify.
The source-visible structural findings are outcome leakage for evaluation purposes; they must be treated as the engineer's reported findings, not as independent model conclusions.

Parent PDF extraction of drawing sheets at original PDF pages 65, 70 and 80 contains garbled glyphs. Plan graphics were visually confirmed in rossdale-drawings.jpg (pages 61, 65, 70, 80); extracted text alone must not be treated as reliable dimensions or annotations.
